content:
- Model consistently overestimates prices in early forecast periods, especially after recent spikes or volatility.
- Forecasts tend to be too high in the first 5–10 days of the 30-day window, then gradually adjust — suggesting a lag in recognizing mean reversion or short-term momentum.
- After a sharp price spike, forecasts often overshoot the true value and remain elevated longer than warranted — indicating failure to account for post-spike correction.
- Model exhibits persistent downward bias in the latter half of the forecast horizon, particularly when true prices show upward momentum — suggesting underweighting of positive momentum or overreaction to recent lows.
- Forecasts are overly sensitive to recent low prices, leading to prolonged underestimation when prices rebound — indicating a failure to recognize mean reversion in the short term.
- Model tends to underestimate prices when the 30-day history contains a strong upward trend — suggesting underestimation of trend continuation or overemphasis on recent volatility.
- Forecasts often fail to capture the “recovery lag” after a sharp decline — i.e., they underestimate the time it takes for prices to rebound from lows.
- Model overreacts to recent volatility, leading to exaggerated forecasts in periods of high noise — suggesting a need to smooth out short-term fluctuations.
